findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard access (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*") to an IAM user, violating least privilege and allowing broad account compromise if the user's credentials are leaked.

findings.issue_category: long-lived static credentials for IAM user
findings.description: Creating an IAM access key for a human/service IAM user produces long-lived static credentials attached to an over-privileged user, increasing risk of credential leakage and misuse instead of using short-lived roles or federated access.

findings.issue_category: standing IAM user with excessive privileges
findings.description: An IAM user is created and directly attached to an excessively permissive policy, rather than relying on roles with scoped, temporary credentials, expanding the attack surface for privilege misuse.
